BURSEVI:v4p174/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r2.claim: The seven severe years are famine, harder for people than captivity or killing; their inhabitants consume the grain stored in its ears, expressed figuratively as years eating it.

BURSEVI:v4p174/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r3.claim: The wording hints that the dream’s thin cows did not literally eat the fat cows; the famine years consume stored grain instead.

BURSEVI:v4p174/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r4.claim: The exception is what people preserve as seed for sowing after the famine.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.claim: Joseph's reply combines three kinds of speech: interpretation by meaning rather than wording, practical advice, and a report of the unseen future eighth year.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r12.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r12.claim: Al-Sulamī reads يأكلون in the third person, meaning people will eat, rather than addressing the listeners.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r13.claim: The phrase seven severe ones omits the word years, understood from the preceding seven years.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r1.claim: The crops ‘eat’ metaphorically because they are consumed during those years, as in describing day as seeing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r2.claim: Taḥṣinūn means preserve and store, deriving from ḥiṣn, a refuge or fortress.

FARRA:v2p46/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p46/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p46/r6.claim: ما قدمتم لهن means the crops you prepared in advance for those years.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#4/r1.claim: Tuḥṣinūn means you preserve or store.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r1.claim: The seven difficult years follow the seven named years; saying 'after that' rather than 'after them' magnifies the preceding period. 'Seven' is understood as years from the earlier wording.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r2.claim: The famine years consume the grain stored for them; attributing eating to years is figurative for what people undergo, and لهن reinforces that personification or matches the dream's imagery.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r3.claim: Some understand 'eating' as utterly exhausting or destroying, as in the idiom that a journey ate a camel's flesh.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#2/r4.claim: The small amount they preserve is what they protect and store for the next planting; the verb derives from the sense of a fortress as protection and refuge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r1.claim: The drought years are called severe because of their hardship; they consume and destroy the food stored for them, except a little saved for seed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r2.claim: The verse attributes eating to the years as an expansive metaphor, and the little reserved is what people protect and store for planting.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r1.claim: In the seven hard years, their people consume the stored grain; attributing eating to the years is figurative and aligns the interpretation with the dream symbol.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r2.claim: They should preserve a small amount for seed.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r1.claim: The seven severe years are famine years, represented by the lean cows and dry ears; their duration follows the two dreams’ imagery.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r2.claim: The famine years “eat” metaphorically through their inhabitants, consuming the grain previously stored for them.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r3.claim: The reserve should last through the famine, with only a small amount kept outside storage for consumption.

DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r3.claim: He glosses what is saved during the famine as what people store up.

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r1.claim: Qatadah says the seven hard years are barren droughts that consume the provisions gathered earlier, except a small amount people store.

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what people preserve as what they put into storage.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r1.claim: The seven severe years are barren years of hardship.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r2.claim: Joseph noticed the first severe year when a man who usually saved half of the food ate his entire portion.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r3.claim: The severe years consume the provisions people had stored for them.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r4.claim: “Except a little that you preserve” means a small amount that you store.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154/r5.claim: The exception refers to a little that people save.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.claim: In the dream's interpretation, cows represent agricultural years, fatness fertility, leanness drought, and ears of grain provisions.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r3.claim: Seven dry ears signify provisions stored across seven years; the lean cows consuming the fat ones represent drought consuming what prosperity produced.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r5.claim: شداد describes drought years through rational metaphor: the years are called severe because hardship occurs in them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r6.claim: يأكلن means “consume” or “use up,” as in Q 4:2; attributing the consumption to years is a rational metaphor because they are the time when loss occurs.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r7.claim: تحصنون means secure and store in granaries; the drought years exhaust the stores except for a little, so the wording urges ample stockpiling.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r6.claim: Joseph’s storage plan lets successive harvests carry the population through the seven drought years, using even the scant produce obtained during famine.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r7.claim: The Prophet prayed for Quraysh to suffer seven years like Joseph’s famine; the hardship began but ended before seven years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r9.claim: The verse makes the years themselves eat by metonymy, since people eat during those years; drought may also be described as consuming and drying vegetation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r10.claim: Arabic descriptions of famine say that a year stripped everything bare, dried stars, meat, and bone.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r1.claim: Taḥṣinūn means to guard and store up, from the word for a protected fortress.

SAMIN-DURR:12:48/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:48/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:48/r1.claim: سبع شداد omits its counted noun, understood from the prior context; assigning eating to the years is figurative, as with the day being bright in 10:67.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233/r1.claim: Grain should be left in its ear because it keeps better and is less vulnerable to spoilage; the following years will be severe droughts.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#2/r1.claim: The years are described as eating what was stored, though people eat during those years, like calling a night asleep.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#2/r2.claim: “Except a little that you preserve” means a small amount you protect and store.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r7.claim: The seven thin cows and dry ears represent seven barren years that consume what was stored during the fertile years.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r1.claim: The coming drought years will produce nothing, and whatever is sown will yield no return, so they consume what they stored.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r4.claim: The years are made the grammatical subjects of eating by figurative attribution, while their people are the actual eaters; yuḥṣinūn means you preserve and store.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r21.claim: The seven severe years are famine years, severe for the people enduring them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r22.speaker: زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r22.claim: Joseph served food for two, and a man ate half and left the rest; when one day he ate it all, Joseph recognized the first of the seven severe years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r23.claim: The famine years consume what the people had stored in preparation for them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r24.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r24.claim: تحصنون means what you store away.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r25.claim: تحصنون may mean what is kept in protected storehouses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r26.claim: A further possibility is that they reserve a little for seed, thereby safeguarding future provisions.

MUQATIL:12:48-51/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r1.claim: The seven severe years of drought consume what Egypt stored, except the little they preserve.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#2/r1.claim: The famine years are said by figurative attribution to eat what their people consume from the stored harvest of the fertile years.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#2/r2.claim: The stores are what the people put forward for those years, retaining only a small amount of what they protect and save.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r1.claim: The seven severe years are the drought years, and saying that the years eat is metaphor for their inhabitants eating the stored provisions.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r2.claim: What was advanced for the years means what people stored for them; the cited poem similarly attributes sleep to night and heedlessness to day while meaning people do those things.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam relates from his father that Joseph noticed a man consume a double portion; when he ate it all, Joseph identified the first of the seven hard years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r4.claim: The word qalīlan is accusative as an exception; the retained little is what people preserve as seed for sowing and thus protect their provisions.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses tuḥṣinūn as guarding or securing provisions; the wording differs but the meaning is the same.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses tuḥṣinūn as storing provisions, which supports the same sense of preserving food.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r7.claim: The verse indicates that storing food until it is needed is permissible.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:48/r8.claim: The passage establishes that an unbeliever's dream can be true and interpreted as seen, especially when it concerns a believer; here it is also a sign and miracle for a messenger.

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r7.claim: The seven severe years are hard years of drought; saying that years eat what was stored is a metaphor attributing people's consumption to the years.

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r8.claim: Iḥṣān means securing or storing something in a protected place, so only a little of the reserves will be consumed.

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.claim: The first seven years are fertile and the next seven years are drought, as indicated by the dream; the forecast of a further abundant year came through revelation, and Qatada says God granted Joseph knowledge of that year.

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.claim: Joseph’s interpretation covers the next fifteen years of Egypt’s agricultural cycle.

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.claim: Joseph advised storing most of the first phase’s harvest so people would have food during the second phase.

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r4.claim: The second phase would be seven extremely difficult years of dearth.

TAB-FULL:v13p190/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r1.claim: The seven severe years are years of drought and famine that consume the food stored during the seven fertile years.

TAB-FULL:v13p190/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r2.claim: The years are rhetorically described as eating, although their inhabitants eat the stored food; the line about day as heedlessness and night as sleep illustrates this attribution.

TAB-FULL:v13p190/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r3.claim: Taḥṣunūn means to secure or store a small remainder; iḥṣān literally means putting something in a protected place, hence preserving it.

TAB-FULL:v13p190/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r4.claim: Qatada calls the severe years drought and says they consume the provisions gathered earlier, leaving only what people store.

TAB-FULL:v13p190/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what you preserve as what you store or secure.

TAB-FULL:v13p190/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p190/r6.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the preserved remainder as what people raise or save.

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r7.claim: Shidad can mean severe because famine is hard on people, or things that attack; the latter better fits the following image of years devouring stored food.

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r8.claim: The wording personifies the harsh years as ravenous predators that pounce on people and consume their stored provisions.

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r9.claim: Ihsan here means securing and storing a small remainder for later use.

TABATABAI:12:49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.claim: The author says interpreters wrongly treat the dream as a forecast of seven fertile then seven barren years; Joseph instead states the required policy for surviving the anticipated famine.

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.claim: The dream depicts the practical measures the king must take for a coming famine: repeated planting, preserving grain in ears, and rationing reserves, rather than simply forecasting years.

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.claim: Cows represent yearly provisions: fat cows picture plentiful harvests from sustained planting, lean cows picture shortages, and their eating the fat ones pictures famine consuming saved food.

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.claim: The green ears represent stores to be saved and the dry ears indicate preserving grain unthreshed; the dream shows the work required to protect food supplies.

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r5.claim: The small amount to be preserved is a reserve and seed for the recovery year; the dream says the lean cows eat the fat ones, not that they consume every last one.

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.claim: A report says Joseph stockpiled the harvests, sold food during famine first for money, then valuables, livestock, servants, property, and land, and finally for people’s freedom; he then freed the Egyptians and restored their possessions and kingship.

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.claim: The author omits many similar reports about the famine economy because most do not directly serve the interpretation of these verses.

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r9.claim: Shidda, solidity, and difficulty are near synonyms; another account lists seven uses of shidda, including time, anger, pain, drink, and the body.

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r10.claim: Iḥṣān is protection, like placing something within a guard or enclosure.

TABRISI:12:47-49/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r6.claim: The seven severe years will consume the stored harvest saved for them; the years are described as eating because the famine occurs during them.

TABRISI:12:47-49/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r7.claim: Eating can also mean using up and destroying something, as in the idiom that a journey ate a camel's flesh.

TABRISI:12:47-49/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TABRISI:12:47-49/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Yusuf prepared food for two; when the guest ate his whole portion one day, Yusuf recognized that the seven severe years had begun.

TABRISI:12:47-49/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r9.claim: They should preserve a small amount from the harvest, since تحصنون means storing and protecting it.

THALABI:v5p227/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p227/r2.claim: The seven severe years of famine will consume most of the food stored during the fertile years, with only a little kept in reserve.

THALABI:v5p227/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p227/r3.claim: The claim that years eat food is personification: as in poetry saying the day is heedless and night sleeps, people are heedless by day and sleep at night.

THALABI:v5p227/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p227/r4.claim: The exception means they will preserve and store a little.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.claim: Exegetes disagree whether Joseph's interpretation came from knowledge God had taught him or direct revelation; the prediction of an unasked-for abundant year supports direct revelation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r1.claim: The seven harsh years are seven difficult years of famine.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r2.claim: “The years eat” is a metaphor for consuming or exhausting what people stored, as Arabs say travel ate a camel's flesh.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r3.speaker: ذي الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r3.claim: Dhū al-Rumma's verse illustrates the metaphor of something consuming or wearing away.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r4.claim: Another explanation attributes eating to the years because eating happens during them, like calling a night “sleeping”; a poetic line illustrates this usage.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r5.claim: إلا قليلا مما تحصنون means all but a little of what you store or protect.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p137/r6.claim: الإحصان means securing something by putting it in a protected place.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r3.claim: Seven difficult famine years, represented by the lean cows, will consume the grain stored for them, except a little kept in reserve.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r4.claim: “What you preserve” means what they protect and store.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:48/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:48/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:48/r1.claim: He says seven years of famine will follow; people will eat the stored grain while preserving a small amount for seed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The following seven years of drought destroy the stored grain, leaving very little.

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.claim: Al-Qummī reports the king’s dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven green ears with dry ones; the cupbearer recalled it after a time, and Joseph interpreted seven plentiful years, seven famine years, then rain.

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the revealed wording is “what you bring near for them” and interprets the following year as one in which people receive rain.

TABATABAI:12:56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56/r3.claim: Al-Ṣādiq reads “they are rained upon” passively and takes yughāth from rain rather than rescue; al-ʿAyyāshī transmits the same interpretation.
